reasons.framework: React provides an extensive ecosystem of reactive state management and UI components, making it well-suited for building the dynamic exam execution interface and readiness dashboards specified in the architecture.
reasons.language: TypeScript guarantees static type safety when interacting with structured backend schemas such as question taxonomies, evaluation responses, and diagnostic reports, preventing runtime errors.
reasons.build_tool: Vite provides lightning-fast cold server start times, optimized Hot Module Replacement during development, and streamlined production builds with zero complex configuration.
reasons.test_runner: Vitest integrates natively with Vite and executes fast, headless component and unit tests directly from the command line without opening browser windows or needing manual intervention.
reasons.package_manager: npm is bundled natively with Node.js, eliminating prerequisites and offering a universally supported dependency management environment for CI and automated agents.
reasons.frontend_folder: Locating the UI under pilot/app/frontend aligns with the modular monolith layout by cleanly separating the SPA presentation layer from the Python backend service code.

alternatives_considered: Vue.js 3 with Pinia as an alternative frontend framework
Jest as an alternative test runner instead of Vitest
Vanilla JavaScript instead of TypeScript for lower initial type-declaration overhead
pnpm or Yarn as alternative package managers instead of npm
risks: Strict TypeScript definitions might require frequent synchronization updates as backend REST schemas evolve across rapid prototype iterations.
State synchronization issues between browser local storage caching and backend session submission during interactive test taking could cause edge-case data loss if network dropouts occur.
